items.title: U2 Salutes Dolly Parton With Recreation of Their ‘Torn’ Duet in NFL Thanksgiving Eve Halftime Show
items.summary:
U2 used its halftime set at the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game to stage a duet with Dolly Parton, pairing a live Bono with a recording Parton made last summer. The 10-minute performance came between halves of the Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, streamed exclusively on Netflix.

The band kept the song count low, playing four: an abbreviated "Sunday Bloody Sunday," the Parton duet "Torn," "Where the Streets Have No Name" and "Pride (in the Name of Love)." During "Torn," images of Parton appeared on three large curtains that dropped around the stage at the 50-yard line, then fell to the field as roughly a hundred extras formed concentric circles around the platform. The Womack Sisters, nominated this year for best new artist at the Grammys, joined the band, singing an interpolation of the Supremes' "Stop! In the Name of Love" woven into the opening number.

Parton's vocal on "Torn" was reported to be the last studio recording she made before her death in August. The song has been described as depicting a family airing its political differences, with Parton in the role of the mother trying to hold everyone together — a fit for the holiday slot. Variety reported that attentive listeners also caught a snippet of "American Obituary," a song from a recent U2 EP referencing the killing of Renee Good by ICE, tucked inside "Sunday Bloody Sunday."

According to Variety, U2's camp brought the Thanksgiving idea to the NFL rather than the other way around, with the timing tied to "Carnaval de Luz," the band's first album of new material in nine years, released Nov. 13 and debuting at No. 4 on the Billboard 200. The booking follows the league's recent run of holiday halftime shows, including Beyoncé's Christmas Day set in 2024 and Snoop Dogg's in 2025.

It was U2's third NFL appearance and first in two decades, after the 2002 Super Bowl halftime show honoring 9/11 victims and a 2006 performance marking the reopening of the Louisiana Superdome following Hurricane Katrina. The band has been in a steady promotional cycle, including a surprise opening at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony at L.A.'s Peacock Theatre on Nov. 14, which ABC will air as a special on Dec. 8.

On Monday, U2 announced 15 North American stadium dates for 2027, adding to previously announced Central American and European shows. That itinerary returns them to SoFi Stadium on Oct. 1 and 2, 2027.

items.title: Wu-Tang Clan Bring Da Ruckus for NFL Thanksgiving Day Halftime Show
items.summary:
Wu-Tang Clan headlined the halftime show at the NFL's Thanksgiving Day game between the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears, running through a set built entirely from their catalog. Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer Chad Smith backed the group on live drums as its members traded verses.

The set list ran through "Bring Da Ruckus," "Triumph," "Da Mystery of Chessboxin'," "Protect Ya Neck," "Method Man," "Shimmy Shimmy Ya," "Ice Cream," "C.R.E.A.M." and "Wu-Tang Clan Ain't Nuthing ta F' Wit." Young Dirty Bastard, son of the late Ol' Dirty Bastard, handled his father's part on "Shimmy Shimmy Ya."

Eminem and his longtime manager Paul Rosenberg put the booking together. As Consequence reported, the two signed a multi-year deal with the Lions last year to executive produce and curate the team's annual Thanksgiving halftime show, which launched with Jack White. "We often like to do things that are both exciting and unexpected. A Wu-Tang Clan Thanksgiving performance in Detroit certainly fits that description," Rosenberg said in a statement shared by the NFL, adding that he and Eminem have been fans since the early '90s.

Lions president and CEO Rich Haddad framed it as a meeting of institutions. "Our Thanksgiving Day Classic is one of the greatest traditions in sports, and Wu-Tang Clan is one of the greatest performers in music," he said.

The performance arrived less than two weeks after the group's induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame alongside Oasis, Iron Maiden, Sade and Phil Collins. It also wasn't their first halftime set of the year — they played Madison Square Garden during Game 4 of the NBA Finals in June.

Wu-Tang has spent much of the past two years touring. The Wu-Tang Forever: The Final Chamber farewell series began in summer 2025, went overseas and then added a North American leg, with Bone Thugs-N-Harmony supporting, before closing in Phoenix on Oct. 4.

items.title: King Crimson Original Drummer Michael Giles Dies at 84
items.summary:
Michael Giles, the original drummer of King Crimson, has died at 84. The band announced his death in a post on its website, which did not give a cause.

"His extraordinary rhythmic imagination, musical sensitivity and highly inventive approach to drumming were fundamental to the band's pioneering sound," the announcement read, as reported by Variety. It went on to credit his "originality, musical curiosity and uncompromising commitment to creative freedom" with challenging conventions and inspiring generations of musicians.

Born in 1942 in Bournemouth, on England's south coast, Giles came up alongside future Crimson cofounders Robert Fripp and Greg Lake. In 1967 he formed Giles, Giles and Fripp with his brother Peter and Fripp; their 1968 album "The Cheerful Insanity of Giles, Giles and Fripp" sold little but set the stage for what followed. Late that year Giles formed King Crimson with Fripp, Lake, multi-instrumentalist Ian McDonald and lyricist Peter Sinfield.

The band's early shows drew enough attention that they opened for the Rolling Stones at Hyde Park in July 1969. Their debut, "In the Court of the Crimson King," folded rock, jazz, classical and avant-garde elements into a record widely regarded as the first true progressive-rock album, with Giles' thunderous rolls and fast, unpredictable rhythms central to its character. Its reach extended to Yes, Genesis, David Bowie, Roxy Music and later acts like Tool and the Mars Volta, and Kanye West sampled "21st Century Schizoid Man" on his 2010 single "Power."

The lineup lasted barely a year. By early 1970 McDonald, Lake and Giles had all left, though Giles and Lake played on the second album, "In the Wake of Poseidon." Giles then made a record with McDonald as McDonald and Giles and went on to appear on sessions with Steve Winwood, Bryan Ferry, Leo Sayer, Kevin Ayers, Neil Sedaka, Yvonne Elliman, Andy Summers, Anthony Phillips and the Penguin Cafe Orchestra, among others.

He released the solo album "Progress, Ghost Dance" with David Cunningham and later Crimson member Jamie Muir, and led the Michael Giles MAD Band, which included another Crimson alumnus, Keith Tippett. In 2002 he joined several former bandmates in the 21st Century Schizoid Band, touring the group's early material. He is survived by his children Tina, Amanda, William, Rosie and Oliver, several grandchildren, his sister Marion and his brother Peter.
